newsitem.title: USA: Selling holders to offer more shares in Vail IPO.
newsitem.headline: Selling holders to offer more shares in Vail IPO.

text.p: Selling shareholders will offer more shares than originally expected in the upcoming initial public offering of Vail Resorts Inc, according to documents filed Monday with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Selling shareholders will sell 7.1 million shares in the IPO, up from an original estimate of 5.5 million shares, bringing the total number of shares to be offered to the public to 12.1 million. Vail will offer five million shares, unchanged from its initial plan.
IPO analysts expect the market debut of the ski company, the largest and most popular ski mountain complex in North America, to sizzle with two points of after-market premiums.
The offering has been boosted by good conditions in the IPO market overall and Vail's status as one of the top players in an industry that could benefit from further consolidation, analysts say.
According to its prospectus, Vail had 1.65 million skier days in the 1995-1996 winter season, the most of any ski mountain in North America.

The shares are expected to price later today in a range of $19 to $21 each for trading tomorrow on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "MTN", according to lead underwriter Bear Stearns & Co Inc.
Other underwriters of the deal are Furman Selz, Goldman Sachs & Co, Salomon Brothers Inc, Schroder Wertheim & Co and Smith Barney Inc.
